tasks.answer: Cards are under the heading 'Failures by error class · 4', in this order: ArithmeticException (47 failing), UnknownHostException/'execution exception' (12), PropertyNotFoundException ${partnerQuota.total} (3), PropertyNotFoundException ${healed eq true or selfHealGhost.total gt #} (22). I would look first at the top card, ArithmeticException 'Error while evaluating expression: ${amount % divisor}': biggest count (47 failing, DLQ 41 jobs), 'last seen 2.4 min ago', and it is first on the page. Each card carries a pill 'ranked by attention' whose tooltip (title text, visible in the accessibility tree; I did not hover) says: 'Ordered by the expected cost of waiting: how recently this class was seen and how fast it is growing — classes that reliably clear themselves soon rank lower, and nothing is hidden.' It does not change my pick: the top card is also the biggest and no card is excused by self-healing except the last one. It does explain why the 22-failing card is last, though (its text says 'usually self-heals').

tasks.answer: Card: code 'UnknownHostException', label 'execution exception', pill 'ranked by attention', summary '12 failing · last seen 2.4 min ago · no resolve-time history · no self-heal history.', link '12 instances', 'DLQ 12 jobs', 'retrying 0 jobs', 'sample: execution exception', engines A and B each with acmeApiOutage v1: 6, plus disabled 'Acknowledge' with '🔒 Requires OPERATOR on every engine in this group — missing on engine-a' and disabled 'Retry group' with '🔒 Requires RESPONDER — you are VIEWER'. My reading beyond the numbers: all 12 are dead-lettered (retries exhausted, none still retrying), so nothing will fix itself by waiting; the page has no history for this class, neither how long past occurrences took to fix nor whether they cleared themselves, so it is not discounted as 'self-healing' and it makes no claim in either direction. It is currently active (seen 2.4 min ago), confined to one definition (acmeApiOutage) across two engines. Not understood: 'no resolve-time history' (resolve-time of what? why none?), 'no self-heal history' (is that bad or merely new?), 'ranked by attention' (what attention is the card claiming?), 'execution exception' as a label (it is generic and says nothing about the cause; the code UnknownHostException is the more informative part), and 'Acknowledge' (what it does).

tasks.answer: 'execution exception' (UnknownHostException) is 2nd; the ${healed eq true or selfHealGhost.total gt …} card is 4th and last. Note the card heading shows 'gt #' while the sample line shows 'gt 0'. The screen's reason, partial: the healed card says '22 failing · last seen 2.4 min ago · no resolve-time history · usually self-heals (12/13 past spells, typically ≤ 1 min) — not the 22 dead-lettered (no retries left) · spiking: 23 in the last 10 min.' and the pill tooltip says 'classes that reliably clear themselves soon rank lower'. So the likely reason is the self-heal discount. But the screen does not show the actual score or weights, and the tooltip also says rank rises with recency and growth, and this card is 'spiking: 23 in the last 10 min' with the same 'last seen 2.4 min ago'. Also it has more failing (22 vs 12), all 22 dead-lettered (DLQ 22 jobs, retrying 0 jobs), which the card itself says self-heal stats do not apply to ('not the 22 dead-lettered (no retries left)'). So the screen explains the direction only loosely and even seems to contradict itself; I cannot tell from the screen alone that the order is justified.

tasks.answer: Low-to-moderate trust as a sole guide. More trust: the pill tooltip is honest that 'nothing is hidden', all cards are shown, and the factors (recency, growth, self-clearing) are named; counts are timestamped 'as of … · just now'. Less trust: (a) the last card is demoted for 'usually self-heals' though its own text says 'not the 22 dead-lettered (no retries left)' and 'spiking: 23 in the last 10 min'; (b) three of four cards say 'no resolve-time history · no self-heal history', so the ordering rests on little data; (c) no score, no 'as of' for the ordering itself; (d) heading/sample mismatch 'gt #' vs 'gt 0' (just display truncation, but shakes confidence). Nothing on screen reports how accurate the ordering has been historically. On a real incident night I would use my own count/recency reading and treat the order as a hint.

tasks.answer: Incidents page (/incidents, 'Incident Ledger · 24') is grouped by status: 'Regressed · 3', 'Open · 3', 'Quiet · 17'. Under 'Open · 3' the order is ArithmeticException, UnknownHostException 'execution exception', then PropertyNotFoundException ${healed eq true or selfHealGhost.total gt #} — so execution exception is still above the healed class, same relative order as the landing page. Same pill 'ranked by attention' with the identical tooltip on every card. Same summary lines: '12 failing · last seen 2.6 min ago · no resolve-time history · no self-heal history.' and '22 failing · last seen 2.6 min ago · no resolve-time history · usually self-heals (12/13 past spells, typically ≤ 1 min) · spiking: 23 in the last 10 min.' Extra on Incidents: a separate line per card, 'no reliable self-heal history yet (0 of 10 spells observed)' with tooltip 'Not enough completed, unconfounded retrying spells have been recorded for this class to show a self-heal rate (minimum 10). This is expected — it is the normal state for most classes for a long time, not a sign of a problem.' and for the healed class the tooltip 'This error class usually leaves the RETRYING state on its own — engine-scheduled retries, no operator action — in 12 of 13 observed retrying spells. The rate describes past retrying spells — standing dead-letter jobs need operator action regardless.' Differences: the ledger adds status buckets and first/last seen (healed class and exec exception first seen Aug 4, 2026, 08:02:54 PM UTC · 101d ago), and the 'Regressed' bucket puts partnerQuota and two other classes above all of them, whereas on the landing page partnerQuota is 3rd, below exec exception and above healed. The ledger page says its own purpose is 'distinct from the Stage-0 triage cards above', but there are no triage cards above on that page. Last-seen times differ slightly (2.6 vs 2.4 min), just poll timing. The page does not say whether order within a bucket matches the landing ranking; it merely happens to.
